official.deadline_note: The scholarship question sits on the admission application form, so the scholarship deadline and the application deadline are the same: the application form closes 5 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2) for studies beginning autumn 2027. All application documents must be uploaded by the separate document deadline of 12 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2). Aalto states: 'You cannot apply for a scholarship after the application period.'
official.application_cycle: Master's admissions for studies beginning in autumn 2027; application period 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027
official.status_note: Aalto's master's admissions page states: 'The application period for studies beginning in autumn 2027 will run from 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027.' On the date checked the round had not yet opened.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Aalto states: 'Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are awarded as tuition fee waivers that cover the full tuition fee. Aalto University Excellence Scholarships do not cover living costs.' Published tuition fees for rights to study beginning on or after 1 August 2025 are, per academic year: bachelor's programmes EUR 12,000 in Business and Technology and EUR 15,000 in Art and Architecture; master's programmes EUR 15,000 in Business, EUR 20,000 in Art and Architecture, EUR 17,000 in Technology and EUR 17,000 for the multidisciplinary programmes Creative Sustainability, International Design Business Management and Urban Studies and Planning.
benefits: A tuition fee waiver covering the full tuition fee for the normative period of study
The scholarship also applies during an exchange period or an internship abroad at another university
The scholarship decision is given at the same time as the admission decision

New bachelor's students who accept their admission offer bindingly and pay within 21 days of the date the acceptance letter was sent receive a separate 25% reduction on the first academic year's tuition fee
eligibility: A student from outside the EU, EEA or Switzerland studying in a bachelor's or master's programme taught in English, who is therefore liable to pay tuition fees
The scholarship question must be answered on the admission application form during the application period; no separate scholarship application exists
Applicants admitted from the waiting list cannot receive a scholarship, because scholarship decisions are finalised before admission results are released
Scholarship candidates are screened against the EU sanctions lists
requirements: Submit the application form in the Studyinfo.fi service during the application period, 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2)
Upload all application documents by the document deadline of 12 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2)
Pay the EUR 100 application fee within seven days of submitting the application if not an EU/EEA or Swiss citizen; the fee cannot be paid late and unpaid applications are not processed
documents: Bachelor's degree certificate, or a provisional certificate if the final one is delayed, with completion and award dates no later than 31 July 2027
Official transcript of study records for the bachelor's degree, including all pages and showing courses, grades, credits and completion dates
Authorised translations of the degree certificate and transcript if not in English, Finnish or Swedish
Copy of passport or official government-issued photo ID showing citizenship
Accepted proof of language proficiency in the language of instruction of the study option
Portfolio in PDF format for study options in art and design and architecture
GMAT or GRE score reports sent electronically by the test administrator for School of Business study options in admission group 2
selection_criteria: Ranking on the study option's published evaluation criteria, with scholarships allocated during the academic evaluation stage in master's admissions
Programmes may decide not to grant any scholarships at all
Applying for a scholarship has no effect on the admission decision either way
coverage: 100% of the tuition fee for the normative period of study: three years full-time for a bachelor's degree and two years full-time for a master's degree
No living costs; Aalto states students must cover all living expenses, at least 800 euros per month, and other study-related costs from their own financial resources

The tuition fee itself covers courses, academic supervision, exams, counselling and services such as student services, library and IT; it does not cover the compulsory Student Union AYY membership fee or the student healthcare fee
application_method: Complete the admission application form in the national Studyinfo.fi service during the application period
Answer the scholarship question on that same form to apply or not to apply for the tuition fee waiver
Upload all obligatory documents and any study-option-specific documents by the document deadline
official.application_route: One form only: answer the scholarship question on the Studyinfo.fi admission application form during the application period; there is no separate scholarship application.
official.citizenship_residency: Most non-EU/EEA citizens are liable to pay tuition fees and are therefore eligible to apply. Citizens of EU or EEA member states or Switzerland do not pay tuition fees and cannot hold the Excellence Scholarship. Holders of certain Finnish residence permits, including a permanent residence card (type P), an EU residence permit for third-country nationals with long-term residence (type P-EU), an EU family member's residence card, an EU blue card, a Brexit residence permit or a permit based on temporary protection, are also exempt.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - students from outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland who are liable to pay tuition fees are the intended group.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applies to English-taught bachelor's and master's degree programmes only; doctoral studies, programmes taught in Finnish or Swedish, and Erasmus Mundus students do not pay tuition fees. Certain international joint degree programmes have their own tuition fees and scholarship schemes and fall outside this award.
official.duration: The normative period of study: three years full-time for a bachelor's degree and two years full-time for a master's degree. The scholarship requires full-time study according to the approved personal study plan.
official.description: Aalto University awards a very limited number of merit-based Excellence Scholarships as tuition fee waivers covering the full tuition fee, granted on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving fee-paying applicants on each programme's evaluation criteria. The scholarship is applied for on the admission application form and decided with the admission decision, and it does not cover living costs.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee waiver awarded with the admission decision

not_confirmed: travel_coverage wording beyond the general statement that other study-related costs are the student's own
verification.notes: Aalto's own scholarships and tuition fees page was read in full, together with its apply-to-master's-programmes page, which supplied the autumn 2027 application period, document deadline, required documents and application fee rules. Aalto publishes tuition fee amounts per field and level rather than a single scholarship figure, so the amount fields are null and the published tariff is recorded in the coverage and tuition-coverage notes.

applicant_utility.summary: The entire application is one tick-box on the Studyinfo admission form, and Aalto states bluntly that you cannot apply for the scholarship after the application period, so the only fatal timing error is finishing the admission application late. Because decision-makers are each study option rather than a central committee, the realistic odds are set by your programme's own evaluation criteria, and Aalto warns that programmes may award none at all. Plan on funding your own living costs in the capital region at a minimum of 800 euros per month, because this award never touches them.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU/EEA applicants to an English-taught Aalto master's programme whose academic record is strong enough to rank at the very top of a small applicant batch.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the evaluation criteria on your chosen study option's own page, not the general admissions page, because that is what the scholarship ranking is based on
Book and sit any required language test early enough that the official score reaches Aalto before 12 January 2027
If you are in School of Business admission group 2, book GMAT or GRE early and have the score sent electronically using Aalto's reporting code
Prepare a separate PDF per study option if you apply to two, including a separate motivation letter and portfolio for each
Pay the EUR 100 application fee within seven days of submitting; Aalto warns it cannot be paid late and unpaid applications are not processed

Confirm your residence permit status, because a fee-exempting permit that is not valid on 1 August means you stay liable for tuition and can keep the scholarship, while EU/EEA citizenship removes it entirely
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the application form but never answering the scholarship question, which silently removes you from consideration
A missing obligatory document after the 12 January document deadline, which causes the whole application to be rejected as incomplete
Being admitted from the waiting list, which permanently forfeits the scholarship because decisions are finalised before results
Applying to a study option that decides to award no scholarships in that round
Uploading documents in the wrong format or to the wrong attachment section, which Aalto flags as a rejection risk
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs of at least 800 euros per month, plus the compulsory Student Union AYY membership fee of 65 euros for academic year 2025-2026 and the student healthcare fee of 36 euros per semester in 2026, plus private health insurance to complement the basic FSHS cover, and any study materials.
document_audit: A Diploma Supplement cannot replace the degree certificate, although one can serve as the translation of it
Transcripts must be original official documents; screenshots from student information systems and links to such services are explicitly not accepted
An expired passport or photo ID is acceptable only if it expired within 12 months of the first day of the application period
If your name differs between your passport and your educational documents, you must upload official proof of the name change issued by a public authority
Only studies completed by 12 January 2027 count in the evaluation, so a transcript improved after that date changes nothing
alerts: Scholarship decisions are study-option specific in master's admissions: a scholarship awarded to your second preference does not transfer to your first, and you lose it if you do not accept the second option bindingly
The scholarship decision cannot be appealed under the Universities Act, unlike the admission decision itself
Aalto reserves the right to change the tuition fees and the scholarship programme, so the tariff published for rights to study beginning on or after 1 August 2025 may not hold for 2027

Do not confuse this award with the EUR 3,000 Pekka Mattila relocation grant for the Marketing and International Management master's programmes, which cannot be combined with it, or with the 25% FUNED and COLFUTURO discounts
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single Studyinfo.fi application form with the scholarship question answered inside the window, documents by 12 January 2027, academic evaluation by the study option, then admission and scholarship results published together on 30 March 2027.
